body:
Throat hit is the sensation of vapor striking the back of your throat as you inhale, and it is one of the most discussed and least understood parts of vaping. Some people want a strong, sharp hit that reminds them of a cigarette. Others find it harsh and look for the smoothest draw they can get. It depends on the nicotine type and strength, the PG/VG ratio, the power and the airflow, the flavor and cooling agents and, importantly, on you. This guide explains what throat hit is, what causes it, how to increase or reduce it, how it differs between disposables, pods and tanks, how to tell a normal hit from a harsh or unpleasant one, what to do if a vape is too strong and how to choose products that match your preference. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## What throat hit is
Throat hit is the scratch, tingle or warmth you feel when vapor reaches your throat. It is a physical sensation, not a measure of quality. It comes from several factors working together: how irritating the vapor is, how hot it is, how concentrated and how forcefully it arrives. Some people associate a strong hit with satisfaction, and others find it unpleasant. There is no right level, only the level you prefer.

## Nicotine type and strength
Nicotine is the biggest contributor. Freebase nicotine gives a sharper hit than nicotine salts at the same strength, which is why freebase is used at lower strengths. Nicotine salts are smooth at high strength, and are used in pods and disposables. Higher strength generally means a stronger hit. See [nicotine salts vs freebase](/blog/nicotine-salts-vs-freebase/) and [nicotine strength guide](/blog/nicotine-strength-guide/). If a vape feels too harsh, a lower strength or salts may help.

## PG and VG
Propylene glycol (PG) gives more throat hit, and vegetable glycerin (VG) feels smoother and softer. A 50/50 liquid has a moderate hit, a high-PG liquid a stronger one and a high-VG liquid a gentler one. See [PG and VG ratios explained](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). Match the ratio to your device, because a thick liquid in a small pod causes other problems.

## Power and temperature
Higher power makes vapor hotter, and hot vapor feels harsher. A coil run above its range can also create burnt-tasting vapor with an unpleasant hit. Lower the power to soften the hit, or raise it for a warmer, stronger one. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## Airflow
A tight airflow concentrates vapor and gives a stronger, more focused hit. An open airflow dilutes and cools vapor, so the hit is gentler. If your device has adjustable airflow, open it for a softer draw, close it for a firmer one. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## Flavor and cooling
Menthol and cooling agents add a cold sensation that can feel like a hit, even without much nicotine. Mint and ice flavors can feel sharper, and sweet dessert flavors can feel rounder. Some flavorings are slightly irritating. If a flavor seems harsh, try another. See [how cooling ice flavors work](/blog/how-cooling-ice-flavors-work/).

## How you draw
A long, hard draw delivers more vapor faster and feels stronger. A short, gentle draw feels milder. Mouth-to-lung style gives a distinct hit, and direct-to-lung spreads it out. See [sub-ohm vs mouth-to-lung](/blog/sub-ohm-vs-mouth-to-lung/). If you are new, take gentle puffs.

## Increasing throat hit
If you want a stronger hit, you could choose a slightly higher strength within what you are comfortable with, a higher-PG liquid, a tighter airflow or a slightly higher power. Change one thing at a time. We do not encourage higher nicotine use: nicotine is addictive, and a stronger hit does not mean a better product.

## Reducing throat hit
If a vape is too harsh, try a lower strength, nicotine salts instead of freebase, a higher-VG liquid, an open airflow, lower power, a flavor without menthol and gentler puffs. Make sure the coil is fresh and primed, because a worn or dry coil causes harshness. See [why a vape tastes burnt](/blog/vape-tastes-burnt/) and [dry hits explained](/blog/dry-hits-explained/).

## Throat hit by device type
### Disposables
Fixed by the maker: usually nicotine salts at about 5 percent in a low-power device, giving a moderate, smooth hit. You cannot change settings, so choose a lower strength or a different flavor if it is too strong.

### Pods
Usually nicotine salts, 50/50, with tight airflow. The hit is moderate. Choose a lower strength liquid if it is too strong.

### Tanks
Freebase at low strength in high-VG liquid, with open airflow, gives a soft hit. You can adjust power, airflow and liquid to your taste.

## Normal versus unpleasant
A mild to moderate scratch or warmth is normal for many users. A sharp burning, coughing, dizziness, nausea or a racing heart is not, and it means something is wrong: strength too high, power too high, a dry coil or a poor liquid. Stop, drink water and adjust. If symptoms continue, seek advice.

## A worked example
You use a 50 mg/mL salt liquid in a pod, and find the hit harsh. You try a 35 mg/mL salt liquid of the same flavor, and the hit softens. You then open the airflow slightly, if the device allows it, and the draw cools. After a few days, you find a combination you enjoy, and you note it down. Changing one thing at a time made it easy to see what helped.

## Common mistakes
- **Equating strong hit with quality.**
- **Raising nicotine strength to get more hit.**
- **Ignoring coil condition.**
- **Changing several settings at once.**
- **Using menthol and high strength together if you are sensitive.**

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does my new vape feel harsher than my old one?
Different strength, ratio, power or airflow. Compare the specifications.

### Does cooling increase nicotine?
No. Cooling agents change sensation, not the nicotine content.

### Does a bigger device have more throat hit?
Not necessarily. It depends on strength, ratio and settings.

### Can I get a hit with zero nicotine?
You can feel a sensation from PG and cooling agents, but it is different. Zero-nicotine products are still for adults.

### What if I cough a lot?
Lower the strength or power, open the airflow and take gentler puffs.

## Shop
Browse [vape juice](/shop/vape-juice/) and [disposable vapes](/shop/disposables/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## How to experiment sensibly
Change one variable at a time, and give each change a few days. Keep a simple note: the product, strength, power if adjustable, airflow setting, how the hit felt on a scale of one to five and what you would change. After a week, patterns emerge. You may find that you like a firmer hit in the morning and a softer one in the evening, which would suggest keeping two products. You may also find that the thing you thought was a strong hit was in fact the cooling agent, and that a plain flavor at the same strength feels smooth. Notes turn guesswork into a method.

## Hit, flavor and satisfaction
Throat hit is only one part of satisfaction. Flavor, vapor temperature, draw resistance and the amount of vapor all contribute. Two products with the same hit can feel very different. If you are chasing a sensation, ask whether it is really the hit you want, or a warmer vapor, a tighter draw or a stronger flavor. Naming what you want helps you choose. For example, if you like a tight draw and strong flavor, a pod system with a salt liquid may suit better than a large open tank, even though the throat hit is similar.

## Temperature and hit
Vapor temperature affects the hit more than many people expect. Warm vapor feels smoother in some products and harsher in others, depending on the liquid. Cool vapor can feel crisp and fresh, but can also bring out a sharp edge in high-strength nicotine. If you can adjust power, try a range of settings, always within the coil's stated range. If you cannot adjust, the maker has chosen the temperature for you, and your options are to change liquid, strength or flavor.

## Hit in different seasons
In cold weather, vapor feels cooler on the way in, and cold air in the lungs can prompt coughing that has nothing to do with the liquid. In hot weather, thin liquid leaks more and vapor feels warmer. If your hit seems different from month to month, consider the weather before you change anything else. Keeping a device in an inside pocket in winter, and out of direct sun in summer, keeps the experience steady.

## When to talk to a professional
If you find that you need ever higher strengths to feel satisfied, or if you have a persistent cough, chest discomfort or other symptoms, speak to a healthcare professional. We are a retailer and make no health claims, and nothing in this guide is medical advice. Nicotine is addictive, and an adult who wants to reduce use can ask a professional for options.

## A last word on comfort
If a product is uncomfortable, change it. Nobody gains anything from putting up with a harsh draw. Try a lower strength, a smoother liquid or a more open airflow, and give each change a few days. Adults who stay comfortable tend to find a routine that suits them, and they avoid the habit of pushing through a hit they dislike.

faq.a: The scratch, tingle or warmth you feel when vapor strikes your throat as you inhale. It is a sensation, not a measure of quality.
Nicotine type and strength, PG/VG ratio, power, airflow, flavor and cooling agents, and how you draw.

faq.q: How do I make it gentler?
faq.a: Use a lower strength, nicotine salts, a higher-VG liquid, open airflow, lower power and gentle puffs.

faq.q: How do I make it stronger?
faq.a: A slightly higher PG ratio, tighter airflow or a little more power. Nicotine is addictive, so do not chase strength.
It adds a cold sensation that can feel like a hit, without more nicotine.
Burning, heavy coughing, dizziness or nausea mean something is wrong. Stop, drink water and adjust.
